_provenance.purpose: Demand check for an AI-built-website launch-checklist article. Taken AFTER a GSC-based read produced the wrong answer: GSC returned four matching queries and the strongest was 'lovable.dev blog' at 29 impressions and 0 clicks. GSC only reports queries the site already appears for, so it cannot measure demand for a topic the site does not cover. That is a survivorship-biased sample, and the same mistake is already recorded in the Hero.tsx positioning comment.
_provenance.no_volume_note: NO_VOLUME_REPORTED is not evidence of no demand. The 14 September capture recorded the same keyword moving from 30/mo to NO_VOLUME_REPORTED in 24 hours at identical settings. Read it as 'no value returned under these settings on this date'.
_provenance.trend_window_note: Every trend array ends 2026-02, seven months before this capture, so the arrays do not describe recent demand and cannot be reconciled against search_volume arithmetically.

_reading.primary_target: `ai built website`, 480/mo at KD 47 with a $28.42 CPC. The phrase describes someone who already HAS an AI-built site, which is the buyer this article is for, and the CPC says advertisers pay real money for that click.
_reading.secondary_target: `website launch checklist`, 140/mo at KD 2 and LOW competition. Low commercial intent at a $4.83 CPC, but close to free to rank for and a natural second phrase in the same title.
_reading.do_not_chase: `ai website builder` at 40,500/mo. The intent is 'give me a builder', the SERP belongs to the builders themselves, and KD 44 against that field is not a fight worth picking.
_reading.limits: Volume and difficulty are one provider's modelled estimates on one date, not measured traffic, and no SERP sample was taken. Do not treat KD 2 as a promise of a ranking.
